title: `plugin-detail` README's "Reference Rail decision matrix" says the rail emits automatically and reads its ≥2-related condition off the objectDef — the shipped synth requires an explicit `showReferenceRail` opt-in and reads `options.related`
body:
Found while repairing `packages/plugin-detail/README.md` for objectui#5174 batch 17 (PR opened from `claude/issue-5174-ungated-docs-batch17`). Filed unassigned and only PARTLY repaired there: that batch had to stop the section contradicting the fenced block it owns, so it corrected the block and the one matrix bullet naming the retired `detail.hideReferenceRail` route. The two prose claims below are a separate defect and were deliberately left for triage.

## What

The README's "Reference Rail decision matrix" states the rail "emits automatically when" four conditions hold. The shipped condition in `packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` is:

```
const willEmitRail =
  options.showReferenceRail === true &&
  !options.hideReferenceRail &&
  Array.isArray(options.related) &&
  options.related.length >= 2;
```

Two mismatches:

1. **"emits automatically" overstates it.** The first conjunct is `options.showReferenceRail === true` — an explicit opt-IN. A caller who satisfies every condition the README lists and does not pass `showReferenceRail` gets no rail. The README never mentions that flag at all, so the page describes a default that does not exist.

2. **Rung 2 attributes the ≥2 condition to the objectDef.** The README says "The objectDef declares ≥2 related collections (lookup/master-detail inbound fields)". The code reads `options.related` — the synth CALLER's option — not the objectDef's inbound fields. The distinction matters to anyone debugging a missing rail: they will go inspect field metadata when the answer is in the `buildDefaultPageSchema` call.

Rung 3 (viewport ≥ xl) is a CSS concern and looks correct. Rung 4 named the retired `detail.hideReferenceRail` objectDef route and was corrected in batch 17 to name the surviving `BuildPageOptions` one.

## Context: this section has already rotted once

Batch 17 also had to replace the section's "Per-object opt-out" example, which taught

```
ObjectSchema.create({ name: 'product', detail: { hideReferenceRail: true } });
```

`ObjectSchema` is not a public export of `@objectstack/spec` (it is an internal bundle symbol), and this package's own CHANGELOG records the objectDef `detail.*` block — naming `showReferenceRail`, `hideReferenceRail` and `hideRelatedTab` explicitly — as an ADR-0085 removed dead read that is "no longer consulted". A repo-wide grep finds zero readers of `objectDef.detail`. That whole route died and the README followed it down; these two prose claims are the part that is still standing.

## Reachability

Documentation only — nothing changes at runtime. The cost is the debugging detour above, and it is the class of defect objectui#5174 exists to stop: the fenced block in this section was invisible to the snippet gate for as long as the page carried an `UNGATED_DOCS` entry, and prose is not gated by anything even now.

Filed by the `domain:devx` os-dev seat, session `session_01MM7kaS4dPpYHV5BsMyu4tQ`, as an out-of-scope finding from objectui#5174 batch 17. A dedup search ran first and found no open card for it.
